decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY recording the 3000 RPM maximum, adjustable 0-to-3000 RPM range, and intended mixing modes.
The basic wiring plan must support the approved replacement motors and their adjustable 0-to-3000 RPM operation.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
That reasoning makes sense. I like having additional power while still being able to control the available speed range.

I’m comfortable with 3000 RPM as long as the motors are not constantly operated at maximum speed. Being able to tune them for different mixing intensities, such as a slow mix versus higher-speed frothing, would actually be ideal.

With the higher RPM, I want to ensure that:
• splashing remains controlled
• mixing stays smooth rather than becoming overly aggressive at higher speeds

If necessary, I’m open to incorporating a splash guard or adjusting the whisk position / bowl depth so the machine operates cleanly.

Overall, I approve of this direction.

value_updates.motor_drive_wiring: The wiring plan must support the approved 3000 RPM motors and adjustable operation from 0 to 3000 RPM.

decisions.reason: The system layout and CAD must accommodate the approved motors, which the accepted proposal identifies as larger than the previously proposed motors.

decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message Event recording that the motors must not be operated constantly at maximum speed and must support prolonged use.

The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY covering controlled splashing at higher speeds and the approved mitigation options.
Approval of a particular motor and speed range does not change the existing strategy of using off-the-shelf prototype electronics.
The source does not change the existing stability or vibration-control requirements; a higher motor speed alone does not establish new stabilization features.
The approved motor speed and splash-mitigation options do not change the existing requirement to prevent liquid from reaching electrical components.
The source addresses motor speed, mixing behavior, and splash control without changing the established dispensing mechanism, sequence, or flow behavior.
The source approves the motor speed range but does not change the standard 120V wall-power decision or establish an incompatible power requirement.
The client merely permits bowl-depth adjustment as a possible splash mitigation if necessary; no bowl dimension or geometry change is required by the source.
